2027 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1X Coupe 3LZ Looks Like a Batmobile, Laughs at $305,000 Valuation
21 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Now that I think about it, why is Robert Pattinson's Batman using an old muscle car as the basis for his Batmobile? The action takes place in modern times. Bruce Wayne would be perfectly capable of buying as many ZR1X Vettes as he likes and turn those into Batmobiles. Then again, those cars would probably be traceable one way or another. See? That's why I'm not Batman. Or am I?
In all seriousness though, the C8 Corvette is a great-looking car. Basically anything higher than a Z06 will offer you this ultra-aggressive widebody aesthetic that you don't necessarily get with the regular Stingray. And when the spec is black-over-black, well, I don't think it gets much better than that to be honest, especially with those $16,000 carbon fiber wheels.
Altogether, this car here retailed for a whopping $261,104 and until yesterday, it had been up for grabs at auction where it failed to sell. The reason why this car doesn't belong to someone else is because the seller, a dealer out of Chicago, refused to let it go for "just" $305,000. I can understand their reasoning. The car could probably fetch $315,000 easily, and people have been unsuccessfully pushing for cheaper ZR1Xs recently at auction.
I guess the market isn't ready to shift just yet on these cars, and sellers can still make a pretty penny on them. Things will change in the next 12 months or so. But not tomorrow, and certainly not today.
Aside from its dark aesthetic, this ZR1X also comes with carbon fiber accents, a rear spoiler, LED headlights, and Michelin tires on those $16k carbon fiber wheels (measuring 20" at the front and 21" at the back). The car also boasts a front-axle lift system with memory settings and Magnetic Selective Ride Control.
Meanwhile, interior highlights include a heated and carbon fiber-trimmed steering wheel, a head-up display, Ultimate Suede Jet Black leather GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilated/power-adjustable), keyless entry, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, and a wide range of electronic driver aids such as lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert, side blind-zone alert, and forward collision alert. The odometer shows 11 miles, so yes, this is a brand-new car.
Photo: Bring a Trailer As for the drivetrain, it's a twin-turbocharged 5.5-liter LT7 V8 , working alongside an electric motor and a 1.9-kWh liquid-cooled lithium-ion battery pack. The combined output is 1,250 horsepower to go with 973 lb-ft (1,320 Nm) of torque. Everything gets sent to all four wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic and an electronic all-wheel-drive system.
I'm sure you already know that this is one of the quickest cars in the world, capable of hitting 60 mph (97 kph) in under 2 seconds flat (as long as we account for the 1-foot rollout).
